# Model and source

* Citation: van der Veer MAA, de Haan TR, Franken LGW, Groenendaal F,
  Dijk PH, de Boode WP, Simons S, Dijkman KP, van Straaten HLM, Rijken M,
  Cools F, Nuytemans DHGM, van Kaam AH, Bijleveld YA, Mathot RAA.
  Predictive Performance of a Gentamicin Pharmacokinetic Model in Term
  Neonates with Perinatal Asphyxia Undergoing Controlled Therapeutic
  Hypothermia. Ther Drug Monit. 2024;46(3):376.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1097/FTD.0000000000001166>
* Original model: Bijleveld YA et al. Br J Clin Pharmacol.
  2016;81:1067-1077 (<https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.12883>), packaged as
  `Bijleveld_2016_gentamicin`.

```{r model-meta}
mod <- readModelDb("vanderVeer_2024_gentamicin")
mod_meta <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
mod_meta$description
mod_meta$units
```

van der Veer 2024 externally validated the Bijleveld 2016 gentamicin model
on 39 new neonates from the PharmaCool Study. The model predicted the new
data well, so the authors merged the model-building and external data sets
and re-estimated the same structural, covariate and variability model on all
86 neonates (Table 2, "Refit: Merged Data Set"). This package entry is that
refit; the original fit remains available as `Bijleveld_2016_gentamicin`.

# Population

The merged data set holds 86 (near-)term neonates (GA > 36 weeks) with
perinatal asphyxia treated with controlled therapeutic hypothermia in 10
Dutch and 2 Belgian NICUs, with 935 gentamicin concentrations (612
model-building plus 323 external; Table 1). Gestational age was median 40
weeks (range 36-42) in both sets; birth weight median 3.40 kg (2.09-5.07) in
the model-building set and 3.17 kg (2.26-4.62) in the external set; 49 of
86 neonates were male. Gentamicin was given as 30-minute infusions of 4 mg/kg
every 24 h (daily dose 3.0-5.9 mg/kg), with concentration-guided adjustment.
Samples were drawn during hypothermia (days 2-3), rewarming (day 4) and
normothermia (day 5).

```{r population}
str(mod_meta$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL per 70 kg) | log(1.88) L/h | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| `lvc` (Vc per 70 kg) | log(33.2) L | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| `lq` (Q per 70 kg) | log(1.81) L/h | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| `lvp` (Vp per 70 kg) | log(32.2) L | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Table 2 footnote, final-model equations |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1 (fixed) | Table 2 footnote, final-model equations |
| `e_ga_cl` (theta_CLGA) | 2.76 | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| `e_sd5_cl` (theta_SD5) | 1.36 | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set; footnote "study day 5 (>96 h postnatal age)" |
| IIV CL | 24.5% -> omega^2 = 0.0582925 | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| IIV Vc | 30.1% -> omega^2 = 0.0867289 | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| IIV Vp | 56.4% -> omega^2 = 0.276188 | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| Cor(CL, Vc) | 0.81 -> covariance 0.0575935 | Not reported in the refit; carried from Bijleveld 2016 Results |
| `expSd` | 0.16 | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set ("Additive error", on log-transformed data) |
| `etaexpSd` (IIV on residual error) | 52.3% -> omega^2 = 0.241792 | Table 2, Refit: Merged Data Set |
| CL = CL x (BW/70)^0.75 x theta_SD5 x (GA/GAmedian)^theta_CLGA | n/a | Table 2 footnote |
| Vc, Vp = V x (BW/70); Q = Q x (BW/70)^0.75 | n/a | Table 2 footnote |
| GAmedian = 40 weeks | n/a | Table 1 (median GA of both data sets) |
| Two-compartment IV model | n/a | Methods, "Original Model" |

# Refit versus original fit

The authors judged a refitted parameter accurate if it differed by less
than 20% from the original fit. The table compares the typical values of
the two packaged models.

```{r refit-vs-original}
theta_of <- function(m) {
  th <- rxode2::rxode(m)$theta
  data.frame(parameter = names(th), value = unname(th))
}
param_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(
  theta_of(readModelDb("Bijleveld_2016_gentamicin")),
  theta_of(mod),
  by = "parameter",
  suffix = c("_original", "_refit")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("^e_wt", parameter)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    original = ifelse(grepl("^l", parameter), exp(value_original), value_original),
    refit = ifelse(grepl("^l", parameter), exp(value_refit), value_refit),
    pct_diff = 100 * (refit - original) / original,
    parameter = ifelse(grepl("^l", parameter), sub("^l", "", parameter), parameter)
  )

param_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(parameter, original, refit, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter,
    "Bijleveld 2016" = original,
    "van der Veer 2024 refit" = refit,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

# Every structural and covariate parameter of the refit lies within the
# authors' 20% accuracy criterion.
stopifnot(all(abs(param_cmp$pct_diff) < 20))
```

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not public. The virtual cohort draws birth weight from a
log-normal distribution centred on the merged-cohort median (about 3.3 kg,
truncated to the observed 2.09-5.07 kg range) and gestational age from 36-42
weeks weighted towards 40 weeks. Each neonate receives one 4 mg/kg dose as a
30-minute infusion at 6 h postnatal age, which is the standard regimen in
both data sets. Postnatal age is supplied on every row (in months) so the
study-day-5 step would fire at 96 h; with sampling to 72 h after the dose it
stays inside the hypothermia and rewarming window.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20241166)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241166)

n_sub <- 200L
hours_per_month <- 24 * 30.4375
first_dose_pna_h <- 6

cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(3.3), 0.17)), 2.09), 5.07),
  GA = sample(36:42, n_sub, replace = TRUE, prob = c(1, 2, 4, 5, 5, 3, 1))
)

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0.25, 2, by = 0.25), seq(3, 72, by = 1))))

single_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cohort |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 4 * WT, rate = 4 * WT / 0.5),
  tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cmt = "central",
    PNA = (first_dose_pna_h + time) / hours_per_month,
    treatment = "4 mg/kg single dose"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim_single <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = single_events,
  keep = c("WT", "GA", "treatment")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Concentration-time profile after a dose (cf. Figure 4)

Figure 4B of van der Veer 2024 is a prediction-corrected VPC of the merged
data set against time after dose. A pcVPC normalises each observation to the
population prediction of its bin, so the simulated percentiles below (no
prediction correction, a single 4 mg/kg dose) are only a qualitative
counterpart: the median falls from about 5-6 mg/L just after the infusion to
below 1 mg/L by 24-36 h, as in the figure.

```{r figure-4}
sim_single |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    p50 = median(Cc),
    p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.3, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after gentamicin dose (h)",
    y = "Gentamicin concentration (mg/L)",
    title = "Simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles, 4 mg/kg over 30 min",
    caption = "Qualitative counterpart of Figure 4B of van der Veer 2024 (pcVPC, merged data set)."
  )
```

## Recommended dosing regimens

The paper concludes that the refit supports the Bijleveld 2016 regimens of
5 mg/kg every 36 h for GA 36-41 weeks and every 24 h for GA 42 weeks, aimed
at a peak of 8-12 mg/L and a trough below 1 mg/L. The typical-value profiles
for a 3 kg neonate are shown for both the refit and the original fit, over
7 days starting at 6 h postnatal age so the study-day-5 increase in CL
(at 96 h postnatal age) is visible.

```{r regimens}
regimens <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("GA 36 wk, 5 mg/kg q36h", "GA 40 wk, 5 mg/kg q36h", "GA 42 wk, 5 mg/kg q24h"),
  GA = c(36, 40, 42),
  interval = c(36, 36, 24)
)
duration_h <- 7 * 24
reg_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, duration_h, by = 0.25))))

make_regimen <- function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  dose_times <- seq(0, duration_h - 1, by = r$interval)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_times, evid = 1L, amt = 5 * 3, rate = 5 * 3 / 0.5),
    data.frame(time = reg_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      id = i,
      cmt = "central",
      WT = 3,
      GA = r$GA,
      PNA = (first_dose_pna_h + time) / hours_per_month,
      regimen = r$regimen
    )
}
reg_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), make_regimen)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_reg <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = reg_events, keep = "regimen") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = "van der Veer 2024 refit"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb("Bijleveld_2016_gentamicin")),
    events = reg_events, keep = "regimen"
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = "Bijleveld 2016 original")
)

ggplot(sim_reg, aes(time, Cc, colour = model)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 8, ymax = 12, alpha = 0.15, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 96 - first_dose_pna_h, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, 24)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)",
    y = "Gentamicin concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Typical 3 kg neonate. Shaded band: 8-12 mg/L peak target; dashed line:",
      "1 mg/L trough target; dotted line: 96 h postnatal age (study day 5)."
    )
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r regimen-targets}
peak_trough <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  dose_times <- seq(0, duration_h - r$interval, by = r$interval)
  sim_reg |>
    dplyr::filter(regimen == r$regimen) |>
    dplyr::group_by(model) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      regimen = r$regimen,
      peak_first = Cc[time == 1],
      trough_first = Cc[time == r$interval],
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}))

peak_trough |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, model, peak_first, trough_first) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Model" = model,
    "Peak 30 min after first infusion (mg/L)" = peak_first,
    "Trough before second dose (mg/L)" = trough_first
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

refit_targets <- dplyr::filter(peak_trough, model == "van der Veer 2024 refit")
# Typical-value check of the paper's conclusion: every recommended regimen
# reaches the 8-12 mg/L peak window and stays below the 1 mg/L trough.
stopifnot(
  all(refit_targets$peak_first > 8 & refit_targets$peak_first < 12),
  all(refit_targets$trough_first < 1)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Single-dose NCA of the stochastic cohort, grouped by treatment. The paper
reports no NCA parameters, so there is no published comparison; instead, a
typical-value solve checks that AUC0-inf equals dose / CL.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_single |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- single_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg", route = "intravascular", duration = 0.5)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

```{r closed-form-auc}
# Typical 3 kg, 40-week neonate, 12 mg (4 mg/kg) over 30 min, sampled to
# 400 h; postnatal age held below 96 h so CL is constant.
typ_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 12, rate = 24),
  data.frame(time = c(0, seq(0.25, 2, by = 0.25), seq(3, 400, by = 1)), evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, cmt = "central", WT = 3, GA = 40, PNA = 1 / hours_per_month)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L)
nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(typ, Cc ~ time | id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 12), amt ~ time | id, route = "intravascular", duration = 0.5),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
auc_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_typ$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::pull(PPORRES)
cl_typ <- 1.88 * (3 / 70)^0.75
c(AUCinf_NCA = auc_nca, dose_over_CL = 12 / cl_typ)
# Same parameters on both sides: only trapezoidal error separates them.
stopifnot(abs(auc_nca / (12 / cl_typ) - 1) < 0.02)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **CL-Vc correlation carried from the original fit.** The refit (Table 2)
  reports the IIV of CL and Vc but not their correlation. The original
  Bijleveld 2016 model estimated r = 0.81, and the refit re-estimated the same
  model, so r = 0.81 is carried forward to form the covariance.
- **IIV converted with omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2).** Table 2 gives IIV as %CV
  without stating the conversion; the log-normal form is used, as in
  `Bijleveld_2016_gentamicin`.
- **Residual error.** "Additive error" 0.16 is additive on log-transformed
  concentrations (the original model), encoded as `lnorm(expSd)`. The 52.3%
  IIV on the residual error is encoded as a subject-level multiplier
  `expSd * exp(etaexpSd)`. (The packaged original-fit model omits this term.)
- **Study-day-5 step.** theta_SD5 applies when postnatal age exceeds 96 h
  (Table 2 footnote); the model derives the indicator from the canonical `PNA`
  column (months).
- **GA reference.** "GAmedian" is taken as 40 weeks, the median of both data
  sets in Table 1.
- **Body weight.** The allometric covariate is birth weight held constant over
  the simulation window, as in the source.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight and gestational age distributions are
  approximations matched to the Table 1 medians and ranges; each subject gets
  one 4 mg/kg dose at 6 h postnatal age.
- **Errata.** No erratum for this article was found when it was added
  (2026-10-29).
